answer: Before filing, the filer must drill a core from the glacier at the vertex where three survey lines meet, and the plume of ice dust it throws up marks the spot. The desk reads the core within a day: its layers must show the real timeline, proving weeks of work, not an hour of fakery. A core with no layers, drilled from the wrong vertex, or a plume no neighbour saw means rejection and the 250-coin bond forfeited, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real cores plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims with forty cores drilled in one afternoon, and all forty showed the same shallow layer.
